historical_basis: Generic hag current research describes old witch/fairy supernatural class (c01/c05/c06/c07). Selects a specifically identified member of that class, Black Annis, as regional exemplar. Leicester City Council's original heritage service directly records blue features and quotes John Heyrick's 1797 On a Cave Called Black Annis's Bower describing vast talons instead of hands. University of Vienna folklore study identifies Black Annis as old hag and quotes Briggs on sharp teeth, long black claws and blue face. Does not transfer this anatomy to all hags, equate it with all goddesses, or claim extra horns/animal body.

prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. ONE square premium painterly folklore encyclopedia illustration of a HAG, selecting the specifically documented BLACK ANNIS regional witch-hag type of Leicestershire. ONE ancient female monster at sandstone cave doorway beneath an old oak. She has visibly BLUE facial skin and, in place of ordinary hands, immense BIRDLIKE TALONS at the end of TWO forearms as John Heyrick's 1797 poem describes, with long dark metallic-black claw digits naturally part of her limbs. Talons large and unmistakably anatomical, not normal fingers merely painted with long nails or gloves. Her old wrinkled face is grim and uncanny, long grey-black disheveled hair. One head, TWO arms ending in talon hands, TWO legs and feet; no generic horns, wings, tail or invented extra body parts. Modest opaque rough brown-grey dress to below knees, both feet visible; talon hands spread at sides clearly visible. Whole figure and claw tips in frame with margin. Malevolent brooding cave-haunter and frightening hag aura, no friendly witch expression. Deep cool blue cave shadows, walnut sandstone, deep forest green oak and restrained antique gold late dusk rim light; refined naturalistic oil-painted textures. No children, victims, blood, skulls, skin garments, attack, gore, nude body, spells, text, inscriptions, signatures, border or watermark. A precise regional hag example, not a claim that every generic hag has blue skin or talons.
